q7.answer: Workers follow the billing_mode flag in the config service, and the charge hold is read from the rollout record before every charge. How quickly they notice a flag change is not known (open point 7). For an invoice in flight, the hold stops any new charge, and in-flight charge calls finish or time out before the flag moves at a charger switch. A worker still on the old flag is stopped by the hold. Charges due in the gap are queued and made late.

q8.answer: The evidence is the rollout record, which sits next to the ledger. It holds the gate counters, the daily comparison results, the time each mode was entered, and the Finance sign-off. A person asks the controller to advance. The controller checks the gate from the record, refuses if it is not met, and only then sets the flag.

q9.answer: The rollout controller detects it. It watches charge outcomes and measures the charge failure rate over any 10-minute window, in both and new_only. When the rate is above 2%, it starts the automatic rollback (RB_Halt) and notifies on-call. It enforces one rollback at a time. There is no minimum sample size, which I flagged as open point 3.

q10.answer: The charge hold is set, so nobody charges. Charges that fall due are put in the charge queue in the rollout record under their idempotency keys, held and not dropped. They are made late, at RB_Handover. The flag is set to old_only, the hold is cleared, and the old engine charges each queued entry that is due and not already in the ledger. How long the hold lasts is not known (open point 6).

q11.answer: Every charge uses the key (customer, billing period). RB_Reconcile matches each charge between the ledger and the payment provider, and the provider is the truth about money moved. A provider charge missing from the ledger gets a ledger entry added. Outcomes that are unknown are looked up at the provider and never retried blind. The old engine checks the ledger before charging at handover, and the provider rejects a repeat key, if it supports idempotency keys. I assumed it does.

q12.answer: Billing stays in the failed step with the charge hold still set, due charges still queued, and the flag unchanged until RB_Handover. Nobody charges meanwhile. The controller retries the step and pages on-call. Each step is safe to repeat, and the controller resumes from the step recorded in the rollout record, including after a restart. A retry limit or escalation after repeated failures was never decided.
